newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-INJURED AUSTRALIA BOWLER BICHEL TO GO HOME.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INJURED AUSTRALIA BOWLER BICHEL TO GO HOME.

text.p: Injured Australia pace bowler Andy Bichel will be sent home after playing just one match on the current Ashes tour of England, the Australian Cricket Board (ACB) said on Thursday.

Bichel has been troubled by a back strain since the team arrived in England last month and was unable to take the field again after playing in a three-day match against county side Derbyshire from May 31.
Team manager Alan Crompton said Bichel had been ordered to rest after consulting a spinal surgeon who diagnosed the injury as a "stress reaction" in his lower back.
"It had been recommended that Bichel should not bowl for three months to ensure a full recovery, putting him out of Australia's Ashes tour," Crompton said in a statement.

Australian selectors called for seam bowler Paul Reiffel to join the squad to compensate for Bichel's injury and a hamstring strain suffered by strike bowler Jason Gillespie in the first test against England last week.
Reiffel arrived in England on Tuesday and will almost certainly be rushed into the side for the second test starting at Lord's next Thursday.
An ACB spokesman said Gillespie's condition was being monitored daily but added it was unlikely the lanky pace bowler would be fit in time.
Crompton said no more replacements would be called in. The ACB's spokesman said Bichel would return home within a week.
England on Sunday won the first of the six Ashes tests by nine wickets with a day to spare.
